lesson.tomorrow: Next time you serve, name the return you expect, then play the one you actually get.

pro.label: Sampras v Agassi, Wimbledon 1999 final
pro.moment: A point from the final: the serve struck out wide to Agassi's forehand, the first volley steered into the open Ad court the serve had created.
pro.read: The serve wins the space before the next swing.

drill.name: Serve and hit the space
drill.how: Serve 10 to each side. Before each serve, say where the return will go. The point only counts if your next shot goes into the space your serve opened.

lesson.cue: Serve the question. Hit the space.

steps.name: Watch both replies
steps.take: Two short replies? Expect a third — but keep watching.
steps.sit: Your wide serves have pulled this returner off the court twice. Watch both returns.
steps.q: Which return should you expect next?
steps.payoff: Two short middle returns: expect a third, but keep watching the ball.
steps.principle: Where you serve decides how much time they have, and what they can send back.
steps.why: Pulled wide, the returner is stretched and can only block it back through the middle. Two in a row is a pattern to be ready for, not a promise.

lines.A: Neither went deep — both came back short through the middle.
lines.B: From that far out, neither was angled — both came back short and central.
lines.C: Both landed short, not deep at your feet.
lines.D: Both came back short through the middle.

steps.name: Your first ball
steps.take: Wide serve, they're still out wide? Hit into the open court.
steps.sit: You serve wide again. They're still stranded out wide, and the return lands short in the middle.
steps.q: Where does your first ball go?
steps.payoff: They hadn't started back yet, so the open court was too far for them.
steps.principle: The serve opened the court. Hit into it while they're still stuck out wide.
steps.why: They're still where your serve left them, not yet running back, so the open court is out of reach. If they were already sprinting back, behind them would be the better ball.

lines.A: Back to their side — they haven't moved, and they punish it.
lines.B: Deep but central — they get back into the point.
lines.C: Into the open court — they can't get across. Point won.
lines.D: The drop sits up — they run it down and punish it.

steps.name: The deep return
steps.unlock: The return has the final say
steps.take: Pinned deep? Reset high and deep, then rebuild.
steps.sit: Same wide serve, but this return is deep and pushes you back on your heels.
steps.q: The return beat your plan. What now?
opts: Hard and deep down the line
steps.payoff: You planned the open court. The return took it away, so reset first.
steps.principle: Plan your next ball before you serve, then let the return have the final say.
steps.why: A deep return takes your time and balance. Playing the planned shot anyway turns their good return into your error. Buy time now; the pattern will come back.

lines.A: High and deep buys time — you're back in the rally.
lines.B: Sharp from off-balance — a fraction off, and it's wide.
lines.C: Hard from deep and off-balance — it sails long.
lines.D: Short, and you're coming in from deep — they pass you.

lesson.title: The Serve Writes the Next Question
lesson.hook: Your serve decides what comes back. Read the reply, then use the space.
